candidate: A question before a recursive command over the project root when sealed files lie on disk below it (kit-native; the gap that README 'Notes and limits' kept until round 4)
what: nn_guard.py reads each command of a line with its own tool, file filters and folder, looks on disk for sealed files below the folder the command sweeps, and asks when one could be read. A command passes when it names folders without sealed files or gives a file filter that leaves them out.
problem_here: grep -r, find, ls -R, tree, tar, zip, cp -r, rsync and their PowerShell and cmd forms passed unasked at the project root, and such a grep can print lines of sealed files.
evidence: The review of 11 November kept this gap; compared with ripgrep 15.0.0 and 15.1, GNU grep 3.0 and findutils 4.10.0 on Windows, 12 and 13 November 2026
cost: A question (a refusal where nobody can be asked) for an unfiltered recursive command at the root of a project whose sealed files are on disk
reason: The project root was the one folder whose sealed files the guard did not look for, so the commonest exploration commands could print sealed data. It asks only when sealed files really lie below, so a project without them on disk sees no change
